# How would you design Shop-ad ranking?

> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/how-would-you-design-shop-ad-ranking)** — free, no card: the interview workspace, an AI interviewer to push back on your design, and the reference solution.

## Problem

Prior experimentation indicates that in certain contexts, an ad that routes a viewer into an in-app Shop converts better than one that sends them to an external website.

Building on that finding, you are asked to design a ranking algorithm for Meta's ads system that can deliberately give Shop ads more prominence — without degrading the user experience and without working against what advertisers are trying to accomplish.

Address each of the following:

* Which objective, or set of objectives, the ranking should optimize for.
* Which features you would feed the model, and which labels you would train it against.
* Whether a hand-tuned boost, a learned ranker, or a multi-objective framework is the right tool here, and why.
* How to serve advertisers whose goals differ from one another — for example, an immediate purchase on the web versus a visit to a physical store.
* How you would validate the design both in offline experiments and on live traffic.
* Which risks, fairness concerns, and cold-start situations deserve attention.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Clarify the objective: balance Shop-ad prominence against user experience and advertiser value, likely as a weighted or multi-task objective.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Feed features about the ad, the viewer, the context, and the Shop destination, with labels like conversion and downstream engagement.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Discuss how you would control the trade-off, such as blending scores, capping Shop-ad exposure, or running online experiments to tune weights.

</details>
